step.name: Driver compilation verification
step.description: Build the V80 FireSim driver binary using the build system. Run 'make -C $FIRESIM/sim PLATFORM=xilinx_alveo_v80 xilinx_alveo_v80' within the conda environment. This compiles simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc against the FireSim MIDAS headers and links it into a driver binary. The driver uses standard POSIX APIs (mmap, pread/pwrite, open) so no special QDMA SDK headers are needed, but verify the conda environment provides all required headers and libraries.
success_criteria: make command completes without compilation errors
Driver binary is produced at the expected output path (FireSim-xilinx_alveo_v80 or similar)
No unresolved symbols at link time
Binary runs with --help or similar flag without segfault (basic smoke test)

parts.description:
Clean stale build artifacts and rebuild the V80 driver binary from scratch using the inner MIDAS Makefile. The existing .o files in the output/build directory were compiled in a different environment (different glibc sysroot at /scratch/raghavgupta/v80-chipyard/) and contain references to __isoc23_strtol which doesn't exist in this container's glibc 2.35. All .o files must be deleted before rebuilding. The generated header (FireSim-generated.const.h) already exists at $FIRESIM/sim/generated-src/xilinx_alveo_v80/xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config/ and must be copied to the build directory. Then invoke the inner Makefile (which is what the outer Makefile delegates to for driver compilation). The exact command sequence is:

1. Set env vars: CHIPYARD=/home/ray/chipyard, FIRESIM=$CHIPYARD/sims/firesim, RISCV=$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/riscv-tools
2. Set paths: GEN_DIR=$FIRESIM/sim/generated-src/xilinx_alveo_v80/xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config, OUT_BUILD_DIR=$FIRESIM/sim/output/xilinx_alveo_v80/xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config/build, OUT_DIR=$FIRESIM/sim/output/xilinx_alveo_v80/xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config
3. Clean: find $OUT_BUILD_DIR -name '*.o' -delete && rm -f $OUT_DIR/FireSim-xilinx_alveo_v80
4. Copy header: cp $GEN_DIR/FireSim-generated.const.h $OUT_BUILD_DIR/
5. Export CXXFLAGS and LDFLAGS matching what driver.mk sets for conda-only platforms (see below)
6. Run: make -C $FIRESIM/sim/midas/src/main/cc driver MAIN=xilinx_alveo_v80 PLATFORM=xilinx_alveo_v80 DRIVER_NAME=FireSim GEN_FILE_BASENAME=FireSim-generated GEN_DIR=$OUT_BUILD_DIR OUT_DIR=$OUT_DIR DRIVER='<driver sources>'

CXXFLAGS must include: -isystem $CHIPYARD/generators/testchipip/src/main/resources/testchipip/csrc -isystem $RISCV/include -Wno-inconsistent-missing-override -I$CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridge/test -I$CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc -I$CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridge -I$CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridge/tracerv -I$CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridge/cospike -I$GEN_DIR -g -Wno-unused-variable -DFIRESIM -O2

LDFLAGS must include: -L$RISCV/lib -Wl,-rpath,$RISCV/lib -lriscv -l:libdwarf.so -l:libelf.so -lz -lrt -Wl,-rpath=$ORIGIN

DRIVER sources (space-separated): $CHIPYARD/generators/testchipip/src/main/resources/testchipip/csrc/cospike_impl.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/testchipip/src/main/resources/testchipip/csrc/testchip_tsi.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/testchipip/src/main/resources/testchipip/csrc/testchip_dtm.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/testchipip/src/main/resources/testchipip/csrc/testchip_htif.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/fesvr/firesim_tsi.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/fesvr/firesim_dtm.cc $RISCV/lib/libfesvr.a $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/chip/src/main/cc/firesim/firesim_top.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/blockdev.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/cospike.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/ctc.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/dmibridge.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/groundtest.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/simplenic.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tracerv.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tsibridge.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/uart.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tracerv/trace_tracker.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tracerv/tracerv_dwarf.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tracerv/tracerv_elf.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/tracerv/tracerv_processing.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/cospike/mem_pool.cc $CHIPYARD/generators/firechip/bridgestubs/src/main/cc/bridges/cospike/thread_pool.cc

Note: Warnings from testchipip and firechip sources (format warnings in cospike_impl.cc, unused-value in firesim_tsi.cc) are expected and pre-existing — they do NOT indicate V80-specific issues. The V80-specific file simif_xilinx_alveo_v80.cc should compile with zero warnings.

parts.description:
Verify the compiled V80 driver binary has no unresolved symbols at link time and passes a basic runtime smoke test. Run four checks:

1. 'file' command: confirms binary is 'ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64'
2. 'ldd' with conda LD_LIBRARY_PATH: confirms all shared library dependencies resolve (libriscv.so, libdwarf.so.1, libelf.so.1, libz.so.1, libstdc++.so.6, libgmp.so.10). Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/lib:$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/riscv-tools/lib before running ldd. Verify NO 'not found' entries appear.
3. 'nm' check: run 'nm <binary> | grep " U "' and verify that all undefined symbols are standard shared library imports (GLIBCXX_*, GLIBC_*, libriscv symbols like _ZN11processor_t*). There should be NO symbols from __isoc23_* (which would indicate stale object files from a different glibc).
4. Runtime smoke test: run the binary with LD_LIBRARY_PATH set. Since there is no FPGA hardware attached, the binary should fail with an assertion 'tmp_id == id' in fpga_pci_check_file_id() (it tries to read /sys/bus/pci/devices/.../vendor which doesn't exist or has wrong value). This is EXPECTED behavior — the key thing is it must NOT segfault (exit code 134 for SIGABRT is acceptable, exit code 139 for SIGSEGV is NOT). The binary should print 'Domain ID not specified. Assuming Domain ID 0' and similar default-parameter messages before the assertion.

Also copy the verified binary to the platform delivery directory: cp $OUT_DIR/FireSim-xilinx_alveo_v80 $FIRESIM/platforms/xilinx_alveo_v80/cl_xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config/driver/
parts.build_command: export CHIPYARD=/home/ray/chipyard && export FIRESIM=$CHIPYARD/sims/firesim && BINARY=$FIRESIM/sim/output/xilinx_alveo_v80/xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config/FireSim-xilinx_alveo_v80 && echo '=== file ===' && file $BINARY && echo '=== ldd ===' && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/lib:$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/riscv-tools/lib ldd $BINARY 2>&1 && echo '=== nm undefined check ===' && nm $BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep '__isoc23' && echo 'FAIL: stale glibc symbols found' || echo 'PASS: no stale glibc symbols' && echo '=== smoke test ===' && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/lib:$CHIPYARD/.conda-env/riscv-tools/lib timeout 5 $BINARY 2>&1; RC=$?; echo "EXIT CODE: $RC"; if [ $RC -eq 139 ]; then echo 'FAIL: segfault'; exit 1; else echo 'PASS: no segfault (assertion failure or other non-segfault exit is expected without FPGA hardware)'; fi && echo '=== copy to platform dir ===' && cp $BINARY $FIRESIM/platforms/xilinx_alveo_v80/cl_xilinx_alveo_v80-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket8GiBDRAMConfig-BaseXilinxAlveoV80Config/driver/ && echo 'Binary copied to platform delivery directory'
parts.done_when: All four checks pass: (1) file shows ELF 64-bit x86-64, (2) ldd shows no 'not found' dependencies, (3) nm shows no __isoc23 symbols, (4) binary exits with code 134 (SIGABRT from expected assertion) NOT 139 (SIGSEGV). Binary is also copied to the platform delivery directory.
